query: Based only on these records, does a reactive-hypoglycemia-linked glucose dip explain this user's recurring 3pm shakiness and irritability?

ev_A.fact: Every day around 3pm I get shaky and irritable until I eat something starchy — it passes within twenty minutes of eating.

ev_B.fact: My continuous glucose monitor shows a dip right around 2:45-3:00pm on most weekdays, matching a pattern my endocrinologist flagged as reactive hypoglycemia.

relational_connector.relation: A felt symptom pattern is explained by a monitored physiological pattern only when the two share the same timing.
excludes: the user sometimes feels shaky in the afternoon
relational_connector.link_broken_change: The next-day activity is replaced with a low-stakes, movable activity.

connector_spans.quote: Every day around 3pm I get shaky and irritable until I eat something starchy — it passes within twenty minutes of eating
My continuous glucose monitor shows a dip right around 2:45-3:00pm on most weekdays, matching a pattern my endocrinologist flagged as reactive hypoglycemia

retrieval_cue.why_it_naturally_retrieves_R: The question about why the 3pm snack need happens asks for an explanation without naming either prior episode.

relation_specificity.nearby_relation: The user's glucose monitor has occasionally shown brief dips at other times of day.
relation_specificity.why_it_does_not_license_C: That fact does not by itself establish that this specific 3pm symptom pattern shares the same timing as a monitored dip.

coactivation_bridge: ev_A establishes the timing and resolution of the felt shakiness; ev_B establishes a monitored glucose dip at the same time of day. Together they support C: A reactive-hypoglycemia-linked glucose dip explains this user's recurring 3pm shakiness and irritability, because the timing of the felt symptoms matches the timing of the monitored glucose dip the endocrinologist flagged.

latent_C.inference: A reactive-hypoglycemia-linked glucose dip explains this user's recurring 3pm shakiness and irritability, because the timing of the felt symptoms matches the timing of the monitored glucose dip the endocrinologist flagged.

answer_contract.target_proposition: A reactive-hypoglycemia-linked glucose dip explains this user's recurring 3pm shakiness and irritability, because the timing of the felt symptoms matches the timing of the monitored glucose dip the endocrinologist flagged.

decision_semantics.yes: Visible evidence supports the target proposition.
decision_semantics.no: Visible evidence does not support the target proposition.

replacement_dialogue.content: My continuous glucose monitor readings have been flat and unremarkable all week, with no notable dip at any particular time of day.
Flat readings all week don't give us a physiological match to point to.

link_broken.connector_change: B-prime preserves the same user, session position, and conversational style but removes the matching physiological pattern.
link_broken.rationale: A plus B-prime no longer supports the original C.

required_elements: state that the visible evidence does not support the target proposition
absence.rationale: Both necessary target episodes are unavailable.
